record.category: premium link generator (free leech of host links)

free_tier.stated: 'Free users can generate up to 5 links per day with a maximum file size of 1GB.' Free speed 'Up to 50 MB/s'; premium 'Up to 100+ MB/s'. 'No registration' required.
free_tier.notes: The FAQ claims 50+ hosters including Rapidgator, Uploaded and Nitroflare. Premium removes both caps (unlimited downloads, no file size limit).

per_object_cap.stated: 1 GB per file on the free tier ('with a maximum file size of 1GB'); no limit on premium.

retention.stated: unverified: the FAQ does not say how long a generated link, or the copy on their server, survives.

egress.terms: Free users download from the leech server at 'Up to 50 MB/s'; no byte allowance is stated for the download itself.
egress.free_allowance: unstated; the caps are 5 links/day and 1 GB/file

record.interface_detail: A single web form: paste the host link, click Generate, receive a premium link. No API documentation was found; a wrapper would drive the form or the resulting page with a browser session.
record.tooling: Nothing published. The FAQ recommends IDM, FDM, JDownloader, wget or curl for the generated link, which is a plain resumable HTTP URL.
record.chaining: Its output is an ordinary HTTP link, so it feeds any downloader or storage relay. 5 links/day at 1 GB is 5 GB/day of ceiling, which is 150 GB/month at best.

limits.value: 5 generated links per day on the free tier
1 GB per file on the free tier

record.limits_note: The FAQ also names the failure mode that limits the service itself: an error occurs when 'the filehost's premium account has reached daily bandwidth limit'. The leech site is itself a free user of the host.
record.binding_note: Five links a day binds before the 1 GB cap does: at 5 links/day the monthly ceiling is 150 GB even with maximum-size files, and 1 TiB/month would need 34 files a day.

identity_cost.detail: 'No registration' is stated in the FAQ and on the front page; no account field appears in the generate flow.

record.reliability_note: The leech depends on the vendor's own premium accounts, so it fails when those hit the host's daily bandwidth cap. Ads fund it, and the generated link is a third-party copy, so availability is the vendor's uptime, not the host's.
record.confidence_note: The caps are quoted verbatim from the site's own FAQ. What is not tested is whether a generation succeeds on 2026-10-23: leechpremium.link did not resolve from this host (DNS failure) and the page was read through network requests.

evidence.proved: 'Free users can generate up to 5 links per day with a maximum file size of 1GB'; 50 MB/s free vs 100+ MB/s premium; 'No registration'
front page offers a paste box and 'No registration required for free users'; names 50+ hosts including Rapidgator, Uploaded, Nitroflare

record.notes: This is the clearest published free cap in the sector: 5 links/day, 1 GB/file, no account. It is not a debrid service and it does not touch usenet or torrents; it only converts host links that the vendor's accounts can still fetch.
